seed_spread_caveat.note: single seed per arm; deltas below this are not distinguished from noise

verdict.reading: On the validation selection metric recall@5 delta -0.0011 (r@15 -0.0037) -- a wash, every budget within the seed sd 0.0107. On test recall@5 rose +0.0303, the largest head signal among the survivors, but recall@15 fell -0.0129: the covariate-shift alignment shifts the filter toward accuracy on the head of the pool it ranks (its global binary discrimination drops, mcc -0.081, auc -0.0745) at the cost of depth. Same helps-head-loses-depth shape as the id-gate, and again not a win on the metric selection is made on.
verdict.overall: NOT SELECTED at this scale: validation recall (the selection metric) is a wash within seed noise, so B is not adopted on its own terms, despite the strongest test-head signal seen (recall@5 +0.030). The alignment is mechanically real -- the filter trades global binary accuracy for head accuracy on the ranked pool -- but on one seed at subsample scale it does not move the validation headline. A multi-seed or full-scale run is the only way the +0.030 test head would separate from noise; worth escalating only if a cheap second seed reproduces the head gain.
